# Full-space logarithmic weights: the same-separator physical density and its exact flux

This note derives a REGULAR, singleton-contact, UNPENALIZED identity. It
uses one separator for body and parameter directions. A parameter-only
separator is not substituted for that separator. The new continuous
logarithmic flux cancels against gradient-labeled VOLUME moments in all
global affine tests. A nonaffine centroid torque remains. No volume
coupling is identified with a surface coupling, and no Gamma payment is
asserted.

The geometric inputs are the actual regular contact/quantile continuation,
the uniform signed energy shape envelope, and actual finite addition of
complete global-cut speeds. The full-space parameter transport and its
gradient labels are independently proved in
`candidate 3b257d8ddacb6167`.
The present note proves why those conclusions can use the SAME eta in the
stated regular joint-response setting. The corrected boundary-flux signs
agree with `candidate 7127f9c7b67df7cb`.

## 1. Exact scope and notation

Let K_z, z in a finite lattice-complete P, be compatible positive convex
d-bodies; let C be their canonical fiber hull, S their sampled union,
dm the mixed volume on S, M=m(S), N=d+1, and g_z the ordinary fiber
centroids. Work relative to aff(P) times R^d. Put

    Sigma=(1/M) sum_z integral_Kz (X-g_z)(X-g_z)^T dX,
    Gamma(u)=sqrt(u^T Sigma u).

The weight is a strictly positive finite-plane concave function

    L(w)=min_r A_r(w)>0 on C,
    A_r(z,X)=b_r+alpha_r.z+c_r.X,
    (1/M) integral_S log L dm=0.                         (1)

It has a positive extension to a common neighborhood of C by the SAME
finite formula. Define E_z(y) as the projective energy and

    f(z,y)=[L(z,y)E_z(y)/M]^(1/N).

Consider an actual unpenalized joint local minimum beta=Q/M. Assume its
chosen proper covering groups have regular cap-mass maps in the full
hyperplane parameters and singleton contact marks Y_i=(p_i,y_i). Their
caps all have actual mass Q. Additional mass-Q pure-base covering rows
are allowed. All old maximizing bases are covered by these groups, with
the exact continuation and strict off-maximizer gaps available. These
are hypotheses; no regularity or supporting-branch reduction is claimed.

For a proper group normalize

    Gamma(u_ij)=1,  sum_j rho_ij=1,
    B_i=sum_j rho_ij/S_ij,
    theta_ij=(rho_ij/S_ij)/B_i,
    delta_i=epsilon f_i/B_i,
    f_i=f(Y_i),   L_i=L(Y_i),   E_i=E_pi(y_i).           (2)

The fixed old cap is

    a_ij.(z-p_i)+u_ij.(X-y_i)>=-epsilon f_i.             (3)

S_ij(z) is its actual fiber coarea, so the continuous-normal flux of
that cap in fiber z is S_ij(z)u_ij. Set S_ij=sum_z S_ij(z).
Regularity excludes unallocated positive-area supporting facets. The
full section-centroid identity is

    sum_z S_ij(z) z = S_ij p_i,
    integral_section X d(coarea)
                 =S_ij[y_i-epsilon f_i Sigma u_ij].     (4)

The own energy denominator is denoted P_i, to distinguish it from L:

    P_i(X)=1+a_i.(X-y_i),
    integral_Kpi P_i^(-N)=E_i,
    integral_Kpi P_i^(-N-1)=E_i,
    integral_Kpi X P_i^(-N-1)=E_i y_i.                 (5)

Here a_i is the ENERGY normalizer. It is not the full buffered-source
normalizer. After the gradient-label argument below, the latter balance is

    sum_j rho_ij u_ij
           =epsilon f_i[a_i+c_i/(N L_i)],              (6)

where c_i=grad_X L(Y_i). Before that argument one may use a selected
continuous supergradient of L at Y_i in (6). Positive separator weight
will force its uniqueness.

## 2. One joint response and one separator

Use an actually addable convex cone of bounded signed radial body speeds
v, with inward speed positive. Complete signed global cuts supply the
needed class. The same proof applies to any smaller actual class. For
parameters it suffices to allow directions h for which h+cL has a finite
concave extension to a common neighborhood, for some c>=0. This includes
both signs of every affine function, both L and -L, and h=-Phi for every
globally finite continuous convex Phi. The finite extension ensures that
simultaneous signed body changes and parameter changes are actual: L+t h
remains concave and positive on all sufficiently close bodies. Merely
postulating independent formal tangent spaces would not suffice.

Define, on the old bodies,

    D=sum_z integral_boundary(Kz) v_z,
    loss_ij=integral_boundary cap-selector_ij v,
    C_i=integral_boundary(Kpi) P_i^(-N) v_pi,
    J_i=sum_z integral_boundary(Kz)
                         sum_j rho_ij[u_ij.(X-g_z)]^2 v_z,
    s(v)=(1/M)sum_z integral_boundary(Kz) log L(z,X) v_z,
    H(h)=(1/M)integral_S h/L dm.                        (7)

Holding RAW L fixed while changing the bodies and then geometrically
renormalizing it gives dot L/L=s(v). With simultaneous raw h the complete
formula at a fixed mark is

    dot L/L=s(v)+h/L-H(h).                              (8)

Indeed the old logarithmic integral is zero, and its shape derivative is
-integral_boundary log L v. This also proves (8) for nested paths without
any signed-extension issue. The uniform signed energy envelope supplies
dot E_i=-C_i. The covariance calculation gives

    sum_j rho_ij dot Gamma(u_ij)=D/(2M)-J_i/(2M).         (9)

Consequently the actual regular-singleton normalized covering derivative
is -R_i(v,h)/M, where

 R_i(v,h)=sum_j theta_ij loss_ij-beta D
  +delta_i[C_i/(N E_i)+J_i/(2M)-(N+2)D/(2NM)
                    -s(v)/N-h(Y_i)/(N L_i)+H(h)/N].    (10)

For an atomic row its response is its whole-fiber cap loss minus beta D;
it has no delta, energy, covariance, or parameter term. The source buffer
and changing covariance are both retained in (10).

Actual addition and simultaneous parameter feasibility make the finite
response image a convex cone. Its exclusion from the open positive
orthant gives ONE separator eta>=0, sum_all_rows eta=1, with

    sum_i eta_i R_i(v,h)<=0                             (11)

for every allowed combined direction. No response-cone closedness or
minimax interchange is used. Write

    e_i=eta_i delta_i  (proper rows only),
    Delta=sum_proper e_i>0,   kappa=Delta/(NM).          (12)

Positivity of Delta is automatic if all separator rows are proper. In a
mixed menu it follows from the separately proved atomic hinge test when
beta times the compressed atomic count is less than one. Alternatively
Delta>0 may simply be retained as an explicit hypothesis here.

The parameter part of (11) is

    sum_i e_i h(Y_i)/L_i >= (Delta/M) integral_S h/L dm. (13)

Affine tests of both signs give equal mass and full first moment for

    mu_V=sum_i (e_i/L_i) delta_Yi,
    dnu_V=(Delta/M) L^(-1) dm.                          (14)

Tests h=-Phi give mu_V<=cx nu_V. Both L moments are Delta. The finite-source
allocation proof in the cited transport source therefore yields a genuine
full-space martingale from mu_V to nu_V. In particular, eta in this
transport is the physical separator of (11), not a separately chosen
parameter-only separator.

## 3. Gradient labels and the exact moments used below

Each positive row of (14) has equality in concave Jensen for L. It is
supported on EVERY affine plane A_r touching L at its source. Two active
planes with different continuous gradients would intersect in a
d-volume-null hyperplane in every sampled fiber. Since the row is a
submeasure of nu_V, which has bounded positive volume density, such a
positive row is impossible. Thus every source with e_i>0 has the unique
continuous gradient c_i in (6).

Away from finitely many fiberwise null hyperplanes let c(w)=grad_X L(w).
On row i, contact with an active source plane gives c(w)=c_i almost
everywhere. Base-only kinks and positive-volume overlaps of contact cells
are permitted. Refining a repeated source into its menu labels causes no
problem: split its row proportionally to the e_i/L_i masses.

For every function chi on the finite gradient-label set, the exact row
mass, barycenter, and L moment give

 (Delta/M)integral_S chi(c(w))(1,w)/L(w) dm
        =sum_i [e_i/L_i] chi(c_i)(1,Y_i),               (15)
 (Delta/M)integral_S chi(c(w)) dm
        =sum_i e_i chi(c_i).                            (16)

In particular, with vector-valued chi(c)=c,

 kappa integral_S grad_X log L dm
                  =sum_i e_i c_i/(N L_i),
 kappa integral_S z tensor grad_X log L dm
                  =sum_i e_i p_i tensor c_i/(N L_i),
 kappa integral_S X tensor grad_X log L dm
                  =sum_i e_i y_i tensor c_i/(N L_i).    (17)

The last two are first physical moments WITH the gradient label. Ordinary
unlabeled full-space moments alone would not establish them when L is
piecewise affine. Identity (16) additionally says that each label's e_i
mass is Delta times its ORIGINAL mixed-volume fraction.

## 4. The physical density, including continuous log normalization

Let W_z(X) be the eta/theta weighted actual inward cap selector, including
eta times the whole-fiber indicator for each atomic row. Collecting the
body terms of (10) gives exactly

 Xi_z(X)=W_z(X)-beta
   +sum_(i:p_i=z) e_i P_i(X)^(-N)/(N E_i)
   +(1/(2M))sum_(i,j) e_i rho_ij[u_ij.(X-g_z)]^2
   -(N+2)Delta/(2NM)-kappa log L(z,X).                  (18)

Thus (11) at h=0 is integral_boundary Xi v<=0. The continuous dependence
of the final term is essential. Replacing it by a fiberwise constant,
or using a_i in place of a_i+c_i/(N L_i) in (6), gives the wrong flux.

For arbitrary convex fibers Gauss--Green applies: log L is Lipschitz on
a common neighborhood because L is positive finite PL. Its first weak
derivative is c(w)/L(w) almost everywhere. There is NO seam measure in
this first derivative. The projective kernels are smooth and uniformly
bounded on the relevant fibers by the optimal-denominator floor.

## 5. Fiber force, affine torque cancellation, and what remains

Set I_z=integral_Kz grad_X log L dX. The exact fiber force is

 F_z:=integral_boundary(Kz) Xi_z n_z dS
     =sum_(i,j) eta_i theta_ij S_ij(z)u_ij
        -sum_(i:p_i=z) e_i a_i-kappa I_z.              (19)

Here the cap contribution has the PLUS sign. It follows by applying
divergence to the actual cap: its internal cut boundary has outward
normal -u/|u|. Equation (5) gives
integral_boundary P_i^(-N)n=-N E_i a_i. The centered quadratic has zero
vector flux, since integral_Kz(X-g_z)=0. Constants and atomic selectors
also have zero vector flux. These facts prove every term in (19).

Combining (4), (6), and the first two identities in (17) yields

    sum_z F_z=0,       sum_z z tensor F_z=0.             (20)

There is also exact cancellation of the full continuous affine moment:

    sum_z integral_boundary(Kz) Xi_z X tensor n_z dS=0. (21)

For completeness, put C_i^u=sum_j rho_ij u_ij u_ij^T. The contributions
to (21), before their sum is taken, are:

    W-beta: sum_i e_i[y_i tensor(a_i+c_i/(N L_i))
                                           -Sigma C_i^u],
    energy: sum_i e_i[Id/N-y_i tensor a_i],
    covariance quadratic: Delta Id/2+sum_i e_i Sigma C_i^u,
    constant: -(N+2)Delta Id/(2N),
    logarithm: -kappa integral_S X tensor grad_X log L dm.

The Q Id terms cancel because every chosen proper or atomic row has mass
Q and all eta sum to one. The continuous section centroid in (4) gives
the displayed -Sigma C_i^u term. The scalar Id coefficient vanishes, and
the final gradient term cancels by (17). This proves (21) without assuming
any unproved cancellation of mixed base/continuous covariance.

Let h_z=n_z.(X-g_z) be the ordinary centroid radial speed. Taking the trace
in (21) and subtracting g_z times (19) gives the exact remaining identity

    sum_z integral_boundary(Kz) Xi_z h_z dS
                              =-sum_z g_z.F_z.          (22)

If the centroid graph g_z is affine, (20) kills the right side. For a
nonaffine graph this is not an affine labeled-volume moment, and the
displayed certificates do not cancel it. In particular, the new log term
has not eliminated the earlier centroid torque: it has precisely supplied
the correction required to preserve (20)--(21).
The fiberwise radial array in (22) need not be compatible when the centroid
graph is nonaffine; a positive formal response there is not an actual descent.

One can also check (22) directly. The logarithmic radial term is

 -kappa integral_boundary log L n.(X-g_z)
 =-kappa integral_Kz[d log L+(X-g_z).grad_X log L].      (23)

Summed over fibers, the first term vanishes by (1). The remaining X term
cancels sum_i e_i y_i.c_i/(N L_i) by (17); its g_z term cancels the g_z I_z
introduced when the cap force is written using (19). All other scalar
terms are exactly

    -Delta+d Delta/N+(d+2)Delta/2
                         -d(N+2)Delta/(2N)=0.

No second derivative of L, and no regularity at its creases, is needed.
All formulas include d=1 with endpoint counting surface measure.

## 6. An equivalent full-space convex-order reading, without recoupling

If the physical cone in Section 2 contains every globally finite convex
physical function as a common signed boundary speed, (18) gives

    integral_boundary Xi Phi<=0

for all such convex Phi. Affine functions and their negatives give equal
mass and first moment for the Jordan SURFACE marginals

    mu_S=Xi_+ d(surface),   nu_S=Xi_- d(surface).

They therefore admit their own martingale coupling. This is not (14):
the marginals and their dimensions are different. Even the gradient
label preservation proved for (14) is not automatically valid for this
surface coupling, whose target may charge a crease or a facet.
This step uses the general compact convex-order theorem proved in
`candidate 6eda5637cc09a539`;
the finite-source allocation proof used for (14) alone does not prove it.

There is a precise additional surface reserve. Put B=-kappa log L and
Xi_0=Xi-B. B has a finite convex extension: extend each -log A_r below
its positive minimum on C by a tangent line and take the maximum. Testing
that extension gives

 R:=-integral Xi_0 B d(surface)-integral B^2 d(surface)
     =kappa integral[log L(w)-log L(w')] d pi_S >=0.     (24)

For each surface row define the actual concavity defect

    d_L(w)=L(w)-E[L(w')|w]>=0.

With L_max=max_C L, Taylor's inequality for log gives the quantitative
split

 R>=kappa integral d_L(w)/L(w) dmu_S(w)
       +kappa/(2L_max^2) integral[L(w')-L(w)]^2 d pi_S. (25)

Unlike volume rows, surface rows need not have d_L=0. Equation (25)
records that extra defect rather than silently transferring volume
contact equality to the surface coupling. Neither (24) nor (25) forces
R=0 or pays a specified cap deficit.

## 7. Scope of the advance

The genuinely additional data over an unlabeled base-volume certificate
are (15)--(17): positive-volume PL contact produces a common continuous
gradient label, with its original-volume mass and full tilted moments.
Those data are exactly enough to cancel the new continuous-logarithm
force and all global affine torques in the SAME physical density. The
nonaffine residual (22), the distinct surface concavity defect (25), and
the difference between the two couplings remain explicit. Supporting
proper rows, multi-contact derivative minima, penalties, and a Gamma
payment are outside this theorem.

The companion `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_fullspace_log_flux_identities_slab_recovery.py`
passes 563 exact scalar, actual-interval, and piecewise-affine logarithmic
seam checks. It checks the component Gauss--Green identities and scalar
normalizations, not a fabricated critical menu or a joint-minimum example.
